question.problem:
The function $f(x)=\frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{kx}+2$ has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}-5).
$$

What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{kx}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{ky}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{ky}+2 \\ \frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{ky} & =x-2 \\ {3}^{ky} & =\frac{5x-10}{2} \\ {log}_{3}⁡({3}^{ky}) & ={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}-5) \\ ky & ={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}-5) \\ y & =\frac{1}{k}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}-5)\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{k}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}-5).$ 

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=1.$
